newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks extend gains by close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks extend gains by close.

text.p: The Australian sharemarket extended its early gains to close higher on Thursday as bellwether BHP found solid support around the A$17.60 level and the gold sector rebounded after the gold price strengthened offshore.

The industrial sector ended in the black but saw potential further gains curtailed by ANZ Bank shares going ex-dividend 24 cents. At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 12.6 points higher at 2,383.3.
December share price index futures were up six points at 2,387, a 3.7 point premium to the index.

While the market finished firmer, traders said there were been few real motivating factors with modest gains adding up to a firmer close on modest volume. "Some stocks became quite thin but I don't think there was anything special about it," said Eric Gale, director of institutions at Ord Minnett.
"The market was probably encouraged by the fact that Wall Street was down 70 points but recovered a lot of it in the last half hour," he said.
Golds shone with takeover speculation about Newcrest generated by newspaper reports suggesting a U.S. bid was likely.

Highlands Gold saw plenty of activity with some players betting on an increased bid from Placer Dome, although Placer Dome corporate advisers said they had no plans to do this, given that it already had effective control of the gold miner.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade was moderate with few features. Total options traded 36,177 (40,670)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 5,865 (7,682)

In other local markets, Australian bonds continue to look heavy, yields spike up again as recent data and inaction on policy by the Reserve Bank weigh on the market. By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.17 percent.

The Australian dollar was under pressure from the crosses in the afternoon, partciularly from an ailing US$/yen and was feeling out lower levels of support. By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the local currency was quoted at US$0.7963/68, down from Wednesday's US$0.7975/80.
